newsitem.title: ZAIRE: U.N. agencies mount search for Zaire refugees.
newsitem.headline: U.N. agencies mount search for Zaire refugees.

text.p: U.N. agencies mounted an aerial search for 80,000 Rwandan refugees in eastern Zaire on Friday and aid agencies accused Tutsi-dominated rebels of trying to achieve a "final solution" by condemning them all to death.

In diplomatic moves as rebels closed in on Zaire's capital Kinshasa, Gabon emerged as a possible venue for peace talks after ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko said he was too sick to travel to South Africa.

Under increasing international pressure over their treatment of up to 100,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees, the rebels said former Rwandan Hutu troops and militiamen evacuated 55,000 from Kasese camp, 25 km (15 miles) south of Kisangani, earlier this week.
A plane with U.N. officials and rebels aboard took off from Kisangani after the rebels permitted it to fly to Ubundu, 100 km (60 miles) to the south to hunt for the refugees.

The refugees' plight is turning into a diplomatic and public relations disaster for rebel leader Laurent Kabila. But rebel officials in Kisangani accused the media of biased reporting and blamed U.N. agencies for not repatriating the refugees earlier.
In Geneva, aid agencies expressed outrage at rebel treatment of the refugees following reports that 30,000 Hutus had fled a camp soon after the exodus of 55,000 from Kasese camp this week.
"Eighty thousand people are condemned to a slow and cruel death. The expression 'final solution' is not exaggerated," said Christiane Berthiaume, spokeswoman for the World Food Programme.
"They (the rebels) want these people to die. There's food over there but these people are starving. If the refugees go into the jungle, they will die. We are powerless," she added.
Kabila told Reuters in Zaire's second city Lubumbashi that he would invite the United Nations and aid agencies to investigate the crisis over Rwandan refugees in rebel areas.
"I seek nothing but the truth about the refugee crisis in Kisangani. I will immediately be asking the United Nations and aid agencies to set up an independent probe team on the saga," he said.

Kabila again repeated denials his forces had slaughtered Rwandan Hutu refugees at a camp south of the eastern provincial capital of Kisangani but said he would accept independent findings and where necessary take action against his troops.

"I will accept independent findings and if there is reason to take action against my troops, I will happily do so. But facts before me suggest my troops only intervened to stop fighting between armed refugees and local Zaireans," he said.
Ephraim Kabaija, head of the Rwandan government repatriation commission, said the majority might die as they were hostages of Hutu extremists and were being forced to march through jungle.
U.N. officials escorted by rebels were shocked to find not a single refugee dead or alive at Kasese camp on Thursday after it was sealed off to aid workers and journalists since Monday.
Tutsi-dominated rebels have seized more than half of Zaire since October but deny accusations they orchestrated a campaign against the up to 100,000 Rwandan refugees south of Kisangani.
The Rwandan Hutus fled Rwanda in 1994 and are collectively accused by minority Tutsis of genocide in Rwanda the same year.
A top Kabila adviser said in Kisangani Rwandan Hutu former troops and militiamen evacuated all the refugees from Kasese including 9,000 said by UNHCR to be in no condition to walk.
The camps at Kasese and Biaro were sealed off to aid workers and journalists from Monday while rebels said they were conducting a military operation after the camps were attacked.
The U.N. Security Council on Thursday harshly criticised the rebels for preventing aid from reaching the Hutu refugees south of Kisangani and obstructing their return home to Rwanda.

In Kinshasa, a presidential spokesman said negotiators were considering Gabon as a venue to break deadlock over the venue for talks between Mobutu and Kabila but confirmation was awaited from all sides.
The meeting has become more urgent for the government as rebels advance on the Zaire capital Kinshasa, the last stronghold of Mobutu's army. They captured three gateway towns this week.
Kabila wants the meeting to be a formal handover of power by Mobutu, who has ruled Zaire since 1965. Mobutu insists it should lead to elections to let people decide who they want to rule.
In Luanda, expatriate mining sources said the Angolan army and Zairean rebels are performing joint military exercises on the Angolan side of the border between the two countries. 251343 GMT apr 97
